atomicity.reason: One obligation (open command within 50 ms of the violating sample); the second sentence only defines how the interval is measured.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: sample timestamp and contactor interface are the stream's own terms and the two measuring points are spelled out.

feasibility.reason: The architecture's budget (10 ms acquisition and evaluation cycles plus one 10 ms actuator cycle, leaving 40 ms) fits well inside 50 ms; this holds under the reading that the overcurrent clock starts when the persistence window completes, which is what the current-path monitor's debounced condition implements.

parent_fit.reason: Directly provides the 'bounded reaction time' the story promises a test bench that forces a cell past a limit: 50 ms from the violating sample to the open command.

unambiguity.reason: 'The measurement sample that first violated a cell-protection limit' has two readings for REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT's persistence-qualified limit, the title measures from 'detecting' the violation while the body measures from the sample timestamp, and the limits covered by 'cell-protection limit' are not enumerated.
unambiguity.suggestion: Align title and body on the sample-timestamp start, enumerate the covered limits, and define the violating sample for the overcurrent limit.

verifiability.reason: The 50 ms bound and both timestamps (violating sample, command on the contactor interface) are concrete for voltage and temperature, but for the persistence-qualified overcurrent limit it is undefined whether the clock starts at the first sample above 350 A or at the sample that completes the 100 ms window, so the same overcurrent test passes under one reading and cannot pass under the other (50 ms is shorter than the persistence window).
verifiability.suggestion: State the start event per limit type, e.g. 'for the overcurrent limit, the sample at which the 100 ms persistence condition is met'.

summary: Strong, parent-aligned timing bound with explicit measuring points, but 'the violating sample' is undefined for the persistence-qualified overcurrent limit and the title and body disagree on where the 50 ms starts.
